source_title: Kotian caps a career-best haul to set up Mumbai’s win

Mumbai’s Tanush Kotian shows the ball after finishing the innings with 8 wickets on the fourth day of Ranji Trophy Match between Mumbai and Haryana at the MCA BKC Ground in Mumbai. | Photo Credit: Emmanual Yogini
Tanush Kotian spun his web around Haryana with career-best figures to set up Mumbai’s third consecutive Ranji Trophy victory, with a bonus point, as the hosts continued their march towards regaining the title at the Sharad Pawar Academy ground on Thursday (October 29, 2026).
Kotian claimed eight for 84 to finish with a match haul of 11 wickets as Haryana was bowled out for 256 at the stroke of tea. Mumbai’s openers, Divyaansh Saxena (30 not out, 25b, 2x4, 2x6) and Angkrish Raghuvanshi (67 not out, 39b, 7x4, 3x6), then made light work of the 97-run target, overhauling it in less than 11 overs.
When Kotian opened the bowling from the pavilion end in the morning, Mumbai needed eight wickets to seal victory, while Haryana had to bat out of its skin to salvage a draw. The off-spinner wasted little time in making an impact, inducing an edge from Yashvardhan Dalal that Sarfaraz Khan pouched safely.
Himanshu Rana, who had retired hurt after being struck on the helmet the previous evening, returned to join the resolute Nishant Sindhu. But Kotian struck again close to lunch, getting one to turn sharply into Rana, whose edge was safely held by Saxena at leg-slip. Sindhu then fell at the stroke of lunch, inside-edging an audacious sweep that wicketkeeper Akash Anand caught cleanly.
Kotian continued to vary his angles cleverly, but Samant Jakhar and Anuj Thakral resisted for nearly two hours. The breakthrough finally came when Kotian, bowling over the wicket, turned one through Thakral’s defence to hit the stumps. The resistance unravelled thereafter, allowing Kotian to register his career-best in an innings and a match.
Mumbai’s openers ensured there was no late drama. Unleashing their T20 strokes against Haryana’s spinners, they cleared the boundary with ease. Raghuvanshi even employed the reverse-sweep effectively against left-arm spinner Sindhu before sealing the win with a swat over midwicket for six off off-spinner Kanishk Chouhan.
HARYANA – 2nd innings: Ankit Kumar c Saxena b Kotian 12, Himanshu Rana c Saxena b Kotian 46, Nishant Sindhu c Anand b Kotian 44, Dheeru Singh c D’Souza b Musheer 2, Yashvardhan Dalal c Sarfaraz b Kotian 14, Parth Vats c Raghuvanshi b Kotian 24, Kanishk Chouhan c Lad b Musheer 18, Samant Jakhar b Kotian 40, Anuj Thakral (not out) 40, Ajith Chahal b Kotian 0, Aman Kumar b Kotian 2; Extras (b-5, lb-6, nb-1, w-2): 14; Total (in 85.3 overs): 256.
Fall of wickets: 1-20, 2-54, 3-75, 4-117, 5-128, 6-165, 7-167, 8-248, 9-248.
MUMBAI bowling: Mulani 16-6-49-0, Kotian 34.3-7-81-8, Avasthi 3-1-11-0, D’Souza 3-0-8-0, Musheer 22-4-75-2, Deshpande 7-1-21-0.
MUMBAI – 2nd innings: Divyaansh Saxena (not out) 30, Angkrish Raghuvanshi (not out) 67; Total (for no loss in 10.4 overs): 97.
HARYANA bowling: Chouhan 4.4-1-0-30-0, Sindhu 5-0-53-0, Vats 1-0-14-0.
